proposal.name: page_size_to_limit_value_1_probe
proposal.hypothesis: Legacy $.params.page_size renames to modern $.params.limit with direct integer passthrough (limit = page_size); querying customer-123 with value 1 on both APIs will return exactly 1 item if mapping holds.
proposal.information_gain: Customer-123 has exactly two records, so value 1 is discriminating: a correctly mapped limit truncates to 1 item while an ignored/misnamed param falls back to default 2 items. Prior value-2 observation is non-discriminating because both correct and ignored params yield 2 items. This paired value-1 test therefore tests the rename causally rather than merely repeating default behavior.

assessment.finding: Both APIs returned 200 with item_count 1 when value 1 applied: legacy /v1/customers/customer-123/orders?page_size=1 returned 1 item and modern /v2/customers/customer-123/orders?limit=1 returned 1 item, matching predicted truncation from 2-item dataset to 1 item
assessment.recommended_next_probe: Query both endpoints with no pagination params to confirm 2-item default baseline, then cross-test limit=1 on v1 and page_size=1 on v2 to verify names are version-specific and ignored when swapped
